why_it_was_a_candidate: Marketed as 'the World Championship Medical and Disease knowledge/problem solving competition for High School students... held annually online... to lower the cost to compete for students throughout the world' — sounded like a genuinely open, worldwide, medicine-category competition, exactly the kind of gap this discovery pass was looking to fill.
verdict: NOT_ELIGIBLE for a Türkiye-based student, verified from the operator's own page, not inferred.
evidence_verbatim: 'Students can only qualify for the IMDO via participation in one of our official partner organizations.' Currently confirmed partner organizations, by country: United States (USMDO), China (ChinaMDO), Lithuania (LitMO), Thailand (ThaiMDO), United Kingdom (UKMDO).
reasoning: This is a genuine national-delegation model (like the TÜBİTAK-routed olympiads), not an open worldwide entry despite the marketing framing — but Türkiye has no partner organization among the 5 currently listed. Applying the exact discipline this lane has used throughout: a 'global/worldwide' claim in marketing copy is not the same as an eligibility rule, and here the actual rule (partner-organization-only) closes the door for Türkiye specifically.
note: Recording the rejection so a future researcher doesn't rediscover this and assume worldwide access from the tagline alone.

Marking UNCLEAR per this lane's explicit discipline for genuinely unresolved cases rather than guessing.
next_step: Direct outreach to the organization to ask whether a Türkiye-based student could be placed in a cross-country group would resolve this — not answerable from public pages alone.
